creativity-fixation/random-stimuli.suggested_rewording: Exposure to other ideas or examples during idea generation can raise idea output, but it can also fix attention on the example; which happens depends on the stimulus. (C, adjacent)
creativity-fixation/random-stimuli.claim: Exposure to randomly selected stimuli (words or prompts unrelated to the problem) during idea generation increases the number and originality of ideas, compared with generating without stimuli.
creativity-fixation/random-stimuli.construct: random entry / external stimulation in idea generation

creativity-fixation/heuristic-prompts.claim: Prompting idea generation with generic transformation heuristics ("reverse it", "make it 10×", "borrow from another field") increases the variety and creativity of generated concepts, compared with unprompted generation.
creativity-fixation/heuristic-prompts.construct: design heuristics / transformation operators; analogical transfer

creativity-fixation/conceptual-combinati.claim: Deliberately combining two distant concepts produces more original ideas than working from a single concept, with originality driven by attributes that emerge from the combination.

creativity-fixation/deferred-judgement.claim: Separating idea generation from evaluation, with judgement deferred until generation is done, increases the number of ideas without reducing, and sometimes increasing, the number of good ones.

creativity-fixation/bad-ideas-criterion.claim: Instructing people to generate deliberately bad ideas lowers self-censorship and yields more ideas, including some usable ones, than instructing them to generate good ideas.
creativity-fixation/bad-ideas-criterion.construct: lowered quality criterion; instruction effects in divergent thinking

creativity-fixation/serial-order-effect.claim: In a single idea-generation run, later ideas tend to be more original than earlier ones.
creativity-fixation/serial-order-effect.construct: the serial order effect in divergent thinking

creativity-fixation/constraint-relaxatio.suggested_rewording: In insight problems, impasses tend to break when the solver drops an implicit, self-imposed assumption about the solution. (B; five consistent experiments from one group)
creativity-fixation/constraint-relaxatio.claim: Impasses in problem solving are overcome when the solver relaxes a self-imposed constraint on the solution, so deliberately removing a constraint makes new solution paths available.

creativity-fixation/incubation-effect.claim: Setting a creative problem aside for a break, then returning to it, increases solutions or ideas compared with working on it continuously for the same total time.

creativity-fixation/incubation-condition.suggested_rewording: Incubation benefits are larger after a longer preparation period, and when the break is filled with an undemanding activity rather than a demanding one; in some studies an undemanding activity also beat rest. (B, adjacent)
creativity-fixation/incubation-condition.claim: Incubation benefits are larger (a) after a longer preparation period, (b) with longer breaks up to a point, and (c) when the break is filled with a low-demand activity rather than rest or a demanding task.

creativity-fixation/sleep-insight.suggested_rewording: Sleeping on a difficult problem, after first working on it, can raise the chance of finding a hidden solution at retest compared with the same time awake; the benefit is confined to hard problems and depends on sleep stage. (C, borderline B)
creativity-fixation/sleep-insight.claim: Sleeping between first exposure to a problem and a later retest increases the likelihood of discovering a hidden solution or rule, compared with an equal period awake.

creativity-fixation/walking-divergent.claim: Walking, compared with sitting, increases divergent-thinking output during the walk and shortly after it.
creativity-fixation/walking-divergent.construct: walking / acute physical activity and divergent thinking

creativity-fixation/time-pressure-diverg.suggested_rewording: High time pressure during idea generation tends to lower creative output; low to moderate pressure need not, and may help some people. (C, adjacent)
creativity-fixation/time-pressure-diverg.claim: Time pressure during idea generation reduces creative, divergent output.
creativity-fixation/time-pressure-diverg.construct: time pressure and creativity (challenge vs hindrance stressors)

ten-bad-ideas.helps: when wanting a good idea is what stops the first one being written; later ideas in a run tend to be a little more original, a small tendency that is unreliable for any one person, and asking for bad ideas is untested craft, so treat the ten as a warm-up and read the later boxes first
ten-bad-ideas.backfires: when "bad" turns into jokes rather than range, or when ten is too few to get past the obvious answers: the studies of later ideas being more original used timed runs of several minutes

forced-connections.helps: when ideas have gone stale and familiar; outside stimuli can lift idea output, but random words themselves are untested, so treat each connection as a prompt to test, not a finding
forced-connections.backfires: when a stimulus fixes attention on itself instead of widening it, as provided examples do in design studies, and during convergence, where unrelated input is noise

constraint-removal.helps: when an unexamined assumption is blocking every option; dropping a self-imposed constraint breaks impasses in puzzle studies, but removing a real constraint on purpose has not been tested
constraint-removal.backfires: when the constraint was doing useful work: constraints can raise creativity as well as lower it, and an idea designed without the constraint may not survive its return

stimulus-die.helps: when the same few ideas keep recurring during a divergent phase; heuristic prompts reduced fixation in one design study, and rolling operators at random is otherwise untested
stimulus-die.backfires: when the face rolled does not fit the problem, when the prompt itself becomes the fixation, and during convergence or evaluation, where random input is noise

incubation.helps: when an open-ended problem has been worked properly before the break and the break is spent on something easy and different; across studies a break helps on average, more for divergent tasks than for insight puzzles
incubation.backfires: when preparation was too short, when the break is filled with demanding work, or when the problem is easy or well-structured: sleep helped mainly on hard problems, and walking lifted divergent but not convergent thinking

step-away.helps: when an open-ended problem has had a proper first pass: setting it aside for a real break, filled with something easy and different, helps on average, more for generating ideas than for insight puzzles
step-away.backfires: when the break is a few minutes of scrolling or other demanding work, when the first pass was too short to have anything to incubate, or when the problem is easy or well-structured
